title: Detentions, Red Profiles, and the One-Point Demand, 22 July – 3 August 2024

entries.title: Background
entries.content: Following the 21 July 2024 Supreme Court ruling that scaled back the quota system, reporting described a relative calm. The curfew eased and mobile internet was restored in stages beginning around 23 July 2024. Within days, the focus of the protests shifted from the streets to the leaders of the student movement. On 26 July 2024, protest coordinators Nahid Islam, Asif Mahmud, and Abu Bakar Majumder were taken into custody by plainclothes police from Gonoshasthaya Nagar Hospital in Dhaka, against the advice of medical staff; their phones were seized. Three more coordinators — Sarjis Alam, Hasnat Abdullah, and Nusrat Tabassum — were detained over the following two days. The Home Minister later said the coordinators had been taken into "custody for their safety."

entries.title: What Followed
entries.content: On 28 July 2024, while in police custody, the coordinators released a video declaring an end to the protests. Other protest leaders and observers widely alleged that the statement was coerced and scripted under duress; that characterization is contested and is recorded here as an allegation rather than a confirmed finding. Mass-arrest figures varied by source and date: one Dhaka-based rights group cited more than 3,000 arrested in Dhaka alone by 29 July 2024, while broader nationwide tallies published by Bangladeshi newspapers placed the number between roughly 10,000 and 11,700 across the full protest period. These figures are reported as reported figures rather than as a single precise count. On 29–30 July 2024, coordinators of the Students Against Discrimination movement urged people to cover their faces with red cloth and turn social-media profile pictures red in protest against the government's declared national day of mourning for those killed; the movement spread widely, including among celebrities. On 31 July 2024, the student movement held "March for Justice" protests at courts, campuses, and streets in Dhaka and other major cities, protesting killings, mass arrests, and enforced disappearances; clashes with police occurred in several cities, with reported injuries. On 3 August 2024, coordinators of Students Against Discrimination announced a "one-point demand" — the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her cabinet — at a mass rally at Central Shaheed Minar, Dhaka, rejecting Hasina's offer of talks at Ganabhaban, and announced that a "non-cooperation movement" would begin the next day. Subsequent chapters cover the period after this announcement.
